displayName: Legal Notice — Copyright Infringement (Cease & Desist + Takedown)

recipient.note: role: primary infringer / intermediary / platform / hosting provider

work.note: category: literary / dramatic / musical / artistic / cinematograph film / sound recording / computer programme. Registration is not mandatory but evidentiary.

mandatoryClauses.name: Ownership of Copyright
mandatoryClauses.description: Establish authorship and ownership chain — original creation, registration (if any), assignment/license trail

mandatoryClauses.name: Originality of Work
mandatoryClauses.description: Affirm that work is original and qualifies for protection under Section 13 of Copyright Act, 1957

mandatoryClauses.name: Particulars of Infringement
mandatoryClauses.description: Identify infringing copy, location (URL/platform/physical), date of detection, extent and nature of copying

mandatoryClauses.name: Statutory Basis
mandatoryClauses.description: Sections 14 (rights), 51 (infringement), 55 (civil remedies), 62 (jurisdiction), 63 (criminal liability) of Copyright Act, 1957

mandatoryClauses.name: Takedown Demand (if digital)
mandatoryClauses.description: If infringement is online, specific takedown demand under IT Act S.79 / IT (Intermediary Guidelines) Rules 2021 Rule 3(2)(b)

mandatoryClauses.name: Cease & Desist + Delivery Up
mandatoryClauses.description: Immediate cessation and delivery up / destruction of infringing copies

mandatoryClauses.name: Damages / Account of Profits
mandatoryClauses.description: Claim under Section 55 for damages or account of profits at owner's election

mandatoryClauses.name: Reservation of Criminal Remedy
mandatoryClauses.description: Reservation of right to lodge criminal complaint under Section 63 (imprisonment 6 months to 3 years + fine)

mandatoryClauses.name: Advocate Details
mandatoryClauses.description: Name and BCI enrollment number of advocate

filingChecklist: Notice sent by Registered Post AD / Speed Post AD

For online infringement, simultaneously serve by email AND lodge takedown notice with platform/intermediary as 'affected person' under IT (Intermediary Guidelines and Digital Media Ethics Code) Rules, 2021, Rule 3(2)(b)
Postal receipts, AD card, email delivery proof preserved
Copyright Registration Certificate annexed (if registered); registration is not mandatory but is prima facie evidence
Originality evidence — drafts, dated working files, witnesses, timestamps preserved
Ownership chain documents — employment contract / assignment deed / license — annexed
Screenshots and notarised / archive.org-archived copies of infringing material preserved BEFORE issuing notice
Hash values / metadata of digital files preserved as forensic evidence
Limitation: Suit for infringement = 3 years from each act of infringement (Article 113 Limitation Act, continuing cause of action)
Suit can be filed where plaintiff resides/carries on business (Section 62 — favourable forum, do not confuse with Section 20 CPC)

sections.description: Acts not constituting infringement (fair dealing exceptions)
Civil remedies for infringement — injunction, damages, account of profits
Rights of owner against persons possessing or dealing with infringing copies
Jurisdiction — district court where plaintiff resides or carries on business
Offence of infringement — imprisonment 6 months to 3 years + fine of Rs. 50,000 to 2,00,000
Knowing use of infringing copy of computer programme — imprisonment 7 days to 3 years + fine
Intermediary liability and safe harbour — basis for takedown demand to platforms

relevantActs.act: IT (Intermediary Guidelines and Digital Media Ethics Code) Rules, 2021

sections.description: Takedown of infringing content within 36 hours of complaint by affected person
Pre-Institution Mediation — exempted where urgent interim relief is contemplated (IP suits routinely so)

validation_rules.description: Work must fall within Section 13 categories — literary, dramatic, musical, artistic, cinematograph film, sound recording
Work must be original — minimum modicum of creativity / skill and judgment (Eastern Book Co. v. D.B. Modak standard)
Where author is not the sender, assignment/license/employment relationship must be established
Address why infringer's use does not qualify for fair dealing under S.52
Typically 7-15 days; for online infringement, parallel platform takedown is recommended
3 years from each infringing act (Art. 113); continuing infringement gives fresh cause of action

promptInstructions: Draft a Cease & Desist Legal Notice for Copyright Infringement under the Copyright Act, 1957.

Cite Sections 14 (exclusive rights), 51 (infringement), 55 (civil remedies — injunction, damages, account of profits), 58 (delivery up), 62 (jurisdiction — plaintiff's place), and 63/63B (criminal liability).

Identify the protected work — title, category (literary/dramatic/musical/artistic/cinematograph film/sound recording/computer programme), year of creation, year of publication, author, and current owner.
Annex copyright registration certificate if registered — but note that registration is not mandatory for protection or suit.
Establish ownership chain if owner is not the original author — assignment deed (S.18), licence (S.30), or employment relationship (S.17).
Aver originality — the modicum of creativity standard recognised in Eastern Book Co. v. D.B. Modak (2008).

Particularise the infringement — exact infringing copy, URL or physical location, extent of copying (substantial part test), nature of use (commercial / non-commercial), date of detection, evidence preserved.
Address any anticipated fair dealing defence under Section 52 (criticism/review, research, education, news reporting) and explain why it does not apply.

Demand: (a) immediate cease and desist, (b) takedown of online content with proof, (c) delivery up of infringing copies and means of reproduction, (d) account of profits OR damages at owner's election, (e) written undertaking on affidavit, (f) costs.
If infringement is online, include a parallel takedown demand citing IT (Intermediary Guidelines) Rules 2021 Rule 3(2)(b) — 36-hour takedown for IP infringement complaints.
Reserve criminal remedy under Section 63 (6 months to 3 years imprisonment + Rs. 50,000-2,00,000 fine) and Section 63B for computer programmes.
State the favourable forum under Section 62 — suit may be filed where plaintiff resides or carries on business; reserve right to seek John Doe / Ashok Kumar orders for unknown infringers.
Allow 7-15 days response window; no statutory cooling-off period.
Use firm and assertive legal language.
Do NOT generate the advocate signature block — it is added programmatically.
